title: CSV download safe for Excel
description: Streamed CSV downloads for server apps: RFC 4180 quoting with CRLF records, formula-injection neutralization, UTF-8 with a BOM for Excel, tenant-scoped rows through an injected cursor-paged source plus a per-row authorize hook, explicit column allow-lists, row and byte caps, RFC 6266 download headers, a PostgreSQL row source and export log, and a Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and the web streams (ReadableStream, ByteLengthQueuingStrategy), TextEncoder, AbortSignal and Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route or call exportCsv from your own route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Declare every exportable column with a key, header and value function; nothing outside that list is written. Set defaultColumns to the safe default set.
Supply a RowSource scoped by requester.tenantId (keyset pages: WHERE tenant = $1 AND id > cursor ORDER BY id LIMIT n); on PostgreSQL use createSqlRowSource with an index on (tenant, id).
Add authorize(requester, row) for row-level rules, canReadColumn for sensitive columns, canExport for the export permission and tenantOf as a cross-check.
Set maxRows, maxBytes and pageSize for your data; onLimit 'error' (default) fails oversize exports, 'truncate' ends them early and reports it.
Apply schema.sql and pass createSqlExportLog(db) as log to keep an audit row per export, or implement ExportLog yourself.
Mount createCsvExportHandler with authenticate(request) from your session; adjust prefix, routes and statusFor to your API, and validate query filters in parseFilter.
limitations: Does not authenticate users or define your permission rules; the application injects the requester, row source and hooks.
Neutralization covers leading = + - @ TAB CR (configurable) on string cells; typed numbers are written as-is. It does not detect formulas after leading spaces or full-width characters.
Headers are sent before the stream ends, so a limit or source failure after the first page aborts the download rather than returning an error status.
No background jobs: very large exports stream synchronously within maxRows/maxBytes; queue and email a file yourself for longer runs.
The SQL source is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite (single connection), with text ids; keyset paging over a non-unique or non-indexed column is unsupported.
Production data volumes, Excel versions other than the BOM/CRLF convention, and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: only declared columns are written; unselectable column → forbidden, unknown or repeated → invalid-columns
numbers never get the formula prefix; rows refused by authorize are skipped
options: routes, statusFor: override paths and statuses (default GET {prefix}/export streams text/csv, GET {prefix}/columns)
bom (default true), lineEnding (default CRLF), neutralizeFormulas, formulaEscape (default leading apostrophe)
maxRows (100,000), maxBytes (50 MiB), onLimit (default 'error' → limit-exceeded, or 'truncate')

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/csv-download.test.mjs tests/csv-download-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: fields with commas, quotes and line breaks are quoted with doubled quotes, and every record ends with CRLF
string cells starting with = + - @ TAB or CR get a leading apostrophe; triggers, escape and opt-out are configurable; typed numbers are not prefixed
output starts with a UTF-8 BOM by default and keeps non-ASCII text intact; BOM and LF endings are opt-in changes
download headers: attachment with an ASCII filename plus RFC 8187 filename* for non-ASCII names, text/csv; charset=utf-8, no-store, nosniff; unsafe names sanitized
rows come only from a tenant-scoped source; authorize and tenantOf drop rows the requester cannot read; only declared, selected and readable columns are written
canExport refuses before any row is fetched; malformed requesters are rejected
maxRows and maxBytes fail the stream with limit-exceeded, or truncate and report it; exactly maxRows succeeds
the stream applies backpressure: an unread export fetches a bounded number of cursor pages; cancel and abort stop fetching
a failing first page rejects before headers with an internal-detail-free source-error; non-advancing cursors and oversize pages fail
HTTP adapter: 200 streamed attachment, 401, 403, 400, 404, 405, generic 500; routes and statusFor overrides; parseFilter validation
schema.sql applies; the SQL source pages by keyset within the tenant, honors ownerColumn and allow-listed parameterized filters; the export log records each run

changes: First release: core streaming exporter, in-memory source and log, PostgreSQL row source and export log, and Fetch adapter.
